def:dcsm.title: $\dcsm(\Gamma)$
def:dcsm.text: For $\Gamma\ge 1$, the law $P$ satisfies $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ if \begin{equation} \Gamma^{-1} \;\le\; \frac{\odds\big(p_0(x)\big)}{\odds\big(p_1(x)\big)} \;\le\; \Gamma \qquad\text{for $P_X$-almost every } x, \end{equation} equivalently $\big|\logit p_0(x) - \logit p_1(x)\big| \le \log\Gamma$, where $\odds(u) = u/(1-u)$.

lem:msm.title: Equivalence with the marginal sensitivity model
lem:msm.text: Suppose the propensity obeys $\textup{MSM}(\Lambda)$, i.e. $\Lambda^{-1}\le \odds(e(x))/\odds(\pi(x,s)) \le \Lambda$ for all $x,s$. Then $P$ satisfies $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ with $\Gamma=\Lambda^{2}$, and the bound is attained: every value in $[\Lambda^{-2},\Lambda^{2}]$ is realised by some admissible $\pi$.

lem:box.title: Box form of the identified set
lem:box.text: Under $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ the identified set for the deployment regression is \[ \I_\Gamma(P_{\mathrm{obs}}) \;=\; \Big\{\, p:\X\to[0,1] \;\Big|\; \plo(x) \le p(x) \le \pup(x) \ \text{ for a.e. } x \,\Big\}, \] with \[ \plo(x) = e p_1 + (1-e)\,\sigma\big(\logit p_1 - \log\Gamma\big), \qquad \pup(x) = e p_1 + (1-e)\,\sigma\big(\logit p_1 + \log\Gamma\big), \] all evaluated at $x$. The set is non-empty, convex and compact; every $p$ in it is realised by an admissible law; and $\Gamma\mapsto\I_\Gamma$ is nested increasing with $\I_1 = \{p_1\}$ and $\I_\infty = \{\,e p_1 \le p \le e p_1 + 1 - e\,\}$ (Manski).

thm:rank-identity.title: Rank identity
thm:rank-identity.text: For every measurable $p:\X\to[0,1]$ with $\pi=\E_\mu[p]\in(0,1)$, \begin{equation} \boxed{\; \AUC(p) \;=\; \frac{\E_\mu\!\big[\,p(X)\,R(X)\,\big] \;-\; \pi^{2}/2}{\pi\,(1-\pi)} \; } \end{equation} In particular, \emph{at fixed prevalence $\pi$, AUROC is an affine functional of the outcome regression.}

thm:sharp-auc.title: Sharp AUROC interval
thm:sharp-auc.text: Let $\I_\Gamma$ be the box of \cref{lem:box}, let $\pi_{\!-}=\E_\mu[\plo]$, $\pi_{+}=\E_\mu[\pup]$, and for $\pi\in[\pi_-,\pi_+]$ define \[ V^{\pm}(\pi) \;=\; \genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{\max}{\min} \Big\{\, \E_\mu[p\,R] \;:\; p\in\I_\Gamma,\ \E_\mu[p]=\pi \,\Big\}. \] Then \begin{equation} \Big[\;\inf_{p\in\I_\Gamma}\AUC(p),\ \sup_{p\in\I_\Gamma}\AUC(p)\;\Big] \;=\; \Big[\;\min_{\pi\in[\pi_-,\pi_+]}\frac{V^{-}(\pi)-\pi^2/2}{\pi(1-\pi)},\ \ \max_{\pi\in[\pi_-,\pi_+]}\frac{V^{+}(\pi)-\pi^2/2}{\pi(1-\pi)}\;\Big], \end{equation} and both endpoints are \emph{attained} by members of $\I_\Gamma$. Moreover: \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] $V^{+}$ is piecewise linear and concave, $V^{-}$ piecewise linear and convex, each with at most $n$ breakpoints; both are computed by a continuous knapsack --- fill $p$ up from $\plo$ toward $\pup$ in decreasing (resp.\ increasing) order of $R(x)$ until the budget $\pi$ is exhausted. \item[(ii)] On each linear piece $V^\pm(\pi)=\alpha+\beta\pi$ the objective is a ratio of quadratics whose stationary points solve $(\beta-\tfrac12)\pi^{2} + 2\alpha\pi - \alpha = 0$; the cubic terms cancel identically. \item[(iii)] Consequently \eqref{eq:sharp-auc} is computed \emph{exactly} in $O(n\log n)$ time and $O(n)$ space. \end{enumerate}

prop:unified.title: A unified class
prop:unified.text: \Cref{thm:sharp-auc} holds verbatim for every functional of the form \[ M(p) \;=\; \frac{\E_\mu[p\,\phi] + c_0 + c_1\pi + c_2\pi^{2}} {d_0 + d_1\pi + d_2\pi^{2}}, \] with $\phi$ identified, the stationary condition becoming $A\pi^2+B\pi+C=0$ with $A=c_2d_1-c_1'd_2$, $B=2(c_2d_0-c_0'd_2)$, $C=c_1'd_0-c_0'd_1$ where $c_0'=\alpha+c_0$, $c_1'=\beta+c_1$. Taking $\phi=R,\,c_2=-\tfrac12,\,d_1=1,\,d_2=-1$ gives AUROC; $\phi=\one\{f>\tau\}$, $d_1=1$ gives sensitivity at threshold $\tau$; $\phi=-\one\{f\le\tau\}$, $c_0=\mu(f\le\tau)$, $d_0=1,d_1=-1$ gives specificity; $\phi=\one\{f>\tau\}$, $d_0=\mu(f>\tau)$ gives PPV. The known fixed-threshold results are thus special cases, and AUROC is the new member.

prop:corner.title: Corner evaluation under-covers
prop:corner.text: Let $\mathcal{C} = [\min,\max]$ of $\{\AUC(\plo),\AUC(\tilde p),\AUC(\pup)\}$. Then $\mathcal{C}$ is contained in the sharp interval \eqref{eq:sharp-auc}, and the containment is strict whenever $R$ is non-constant on $\{x:\delta(x)>0\}$. Consequently there exist laws in $\I_\Gamma$ whose AUROC lies outside $\mathcal{C}$, and $\mathcal{C}$ fails to cover the truth.

thm:dcl.title: Decision-censored ERM
thm:dcl.text: Let $\ell(\cdot,y)$ be convex for each $y$ and define the \emph{label gap} $g_\ell(z) = |\ell(z,1)-\ell(z,0)|$. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item[(a)] \textup{(Exact reduction.)} \begin{equation} \Rbar_\Gamma(f) \;:=\; \sup_{P\in\I_\Gamma} R_P(f) \;=\; \underbrace{\E\Big[\tilde p(X)\,\ell_1 + \big(1-\tilde p(X)\big)\ell_0\Big]} _{\text{risk at the midpoint model}} \;+\; \underbrace{\tfrac12\,\E\Big[\delta(X)\,g_\ell\big(f(X)\big)\Big]} _{\text{margin penalty $\times$ identification width}} . \end{equation} For the logistic loss $\ell(z,1)-\ell(z,0) = -z$ exactly, so the penalty is $\tfrac12\E[\delta(X)\,|f(X)|]$: an $L_1$ penalty on the \emph{score}, weighted by how censored each region of covariate space is. \item[(b)] \textup{(Exact convexity --- no relaxation needed.)} $\Rbar_\Gamma$ is a pointwise supremum of functions convex in $z$, hence convex in $z$; over any convex class $\F$ of real-valued scores, \eqref{eq:dcl} is an exactly convex program. Separately, the penalty term of \eqref{eq:wc-decomp} is convex on its own \emph{iff} $g_\ell$ is convex --- true for the logistic, squared and exponential losses, false for the hinge. The distinction matters only for modular implementation, not for tractability. \item[(c)] \textup{(Saddle point.)} $R_P(f)$ is convex in $f$ and linear, hence concave, in $p$, over a convex compact set, so by Sion's theorem \citep{sion1958general} $\inf_f\sup_P = \sup_P\inf_f$ and a saddle point $(\hat f, P^\star)$ exists. The adversary's best response is the explicit vertex \[ p^\star(x) \;=\; \pup(x)\ \text{ if } \ell(f(x),1)\ge\ell(f(x),0), \qquad \plo(x) \text{ otherwise,} \] --- for the logistic loss, $\pup$ exactly where the model predicts negative. $\hat f$ is thus the Bayes predictor for the least-favourable member of the identified set. \item[(d)] \textup{(Bayes act.)} For the logistic loss the pointwise minimiser of \eqref{eq:wc-decomp} is \begin{equation} f^\star_\Gamma(x) \;=\; \begin{cases} \logit \plo(x), & \plo(x) > \tfrac12,\\[2pt] \logit \pup(x), & \pup(x) < \tfrac12,\\[2pt] 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \end{equation} \end{enumerate}

prop:regret.title: Minimax-regret rule
prop:regret.text: Let $H(u) = -u\log u - (1-u)\log(1-u)$. The pointwise minimax-regret score is \begin{equation} \boxed{\; \logit q^\star(x) \;=\; \frac{H\big(\plo(x)\big) - H\big(\pup(x)\big)}{\pup(x)-\plo(x)}\;} \end{equation} with the convention $q^\star = p$ when $\plo=\pup=p$. The value of the game is $\KL(\plo\|q^\star) = \KL(\pup\|q^\star)$.

cor:validity.title: Validity of the certificate
cor:validity.text: If the true law satisfies $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ then $R_{P}(f) \le \Rbar_\Gamma(f)$ for every $f$. The certified number is therefore an upper bound on the risk actually incurred at deployment --- something no observed-data metric provides.

thm:impossible.title: Impossibility
thm:impossible.text: Fix $\eta\in(0,1)$, a loss $\ell$, a score $f$ and $\Gamma>1$. Let $\mathcal{P}_{\Gamma,\eta}$ be the set of laws satisfying $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ with $\Prb(T=0)\ge\eta$. Then for \emph{every} sample size $n$ and every estimator $\hat R_n$ measurable with respect to $\{O_i\}_{i\le n}$, \begin{equation} \sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\Gamma,\eta}} \Prb_P\!\left(\big|\hat R_n - R_P(f)\big| \;\ge\; \tfrac{\Delta}{2}\right) \;\ge\; \tfrac12, \qquad \Delta \;=\; \eta\,\frac{\Gamma-1}{\Gamma+1}\, \E\big[g_\ell(f(X))\,\big|\,T=0\big], \end{equation} where $g_\ell(z)=|\ell(z,1)-\ell(z,0)|$. Consequently no estimator is consistent for the deployment risk uniformly over $\bigcup_{\Gamma\ge1}\mathcal{P}_{\Gamma,\eta}$, and the error cannot be made smaller than a constant depending on $\Gamma$ and the censoring rate.

cor:gamma-unidentified.title: $\Gamma$ is not identified
cor:gamma-unidentified.text: For any $1\le\Gamma<\Gamma'$, the set of observed-data laws compatible with $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ equals the set compatible with $\dcsm(\Gamma')$ --- namely all of them. No test based on $(X,T,TY)$ has power against $\dcsm(\Gamma)$.

ass:iv.title: Leniency instrument
ass:iv.text: $Z$ indexes decision makers, $Z \perp (Y,S)\mid X$ (random assignment and exclusion), and $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ holds conditionally on each $Z=z$.

prop:falsify.title: Identified lower bound on $\Gamma$
prop:falsify.text: Under \cref{ass:iv}, $p(x)$ does not depend on $z$ while $e_z(x)$ and $p_{1,z}(x)$ do, so \[ p(x) \;\in\; \bigcap_{z}\;\big[\plo^{\,\Gamma}_z(x),\ \pup^{\,\Gamma}_z(x)\big]. \] The intervals are nested increasing and continuous in $\Gamma$, hence \[ \Gamma_{\min}(x) \;=\; \inf\Big\{\Gamma\ge1 \;:\; \textstyle\bigcap_z \big[\plo^{\,\Gamma}_z(x),\pup^{\,\Gamma}_z(x)\big] \neq \emptyset \Big\} \] is well defined, identified, computable by bisection, and satisfies $\Gamma_{\min}(x)\le\Gamma_0$. $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ is \emph{refuted} for every $\Gamma < \sup_x \Gamma_{\min}(x)$.

thm:generalization.title: Excess worst-case risk
thm:generalization.text: Assume $\ell$ is $L$-Lipschitz in its first argument with $\sup_{|z|\le B,y}\ell(z,y)\le \ell_{\max}(B)$. Then with probability at least $1-\delta$ over the sample, \begin{equation} \Rbar_\Gamma(\hat f) - \inf_{f\in\F}\Rbar_\Gamma(f) \;\le\; 4L\,\Rad_n(\F) \;+\; 2\,\ell_{\max}(B)\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}} \;+\; 2\,\kappa(B)\Big(\|\hat e - e\|_{L^1(\mu)} + \tfrac14\|\hat\eta_1-\eta_1\|_{L^1(\mu)}\Big), \end{equation} where $\eta_1 = \logit p_1$ and $\kappa(B)=\sup_{|z|\le B} g_\ell(z)$. For the logistic loss $L=1$, $\ell_{\max}(B)\le\log 2 + B$ and $\kappa(B)=B$.

cor:loggamma.title: $\log\Gamma$ scaling
cor:loggamma.text: With $B=B_0+\log\Gamma$ and the logistic loss, \begin{equation} \Rbar_\Gamma(\hat f) - \inf_{f\in\F_\Gamma}\Rbar_\Gamma(f) \;\le\; 4\,\Rad_n(\F_\Gamma) \;+\; 2\big(\log 2 + B_0 + \log\Gamma\big)\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}} \;+\; 2\big(B_0+\log\Gamma\big)\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{nuis}}, \end{equation} i.e.\ the complexity term is \textbf{linear in $\log\Gamma$}, not in $\Gamma$.

prop:lower-gen.title: The $\log\Gamma$ dependence is necessary
prop:lower-gen.text: There is a family of instances and a class $\F_\Gamma$ of constant scores with $\|f\|_\infty\le B_0+\log\Gamma$ for which every estimator suffers excess worst-case risk $\Omega\big(\log\Gamma\cdot n^{-1/2}\big)$. Hence \eqref{eq:loggamma} is tight in its $\Gamma$-dependence up to constants.

cor:uq.title: The two-way decomposition is biased by at least the censoring term
cor:uq.text: Assume $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ and fix $x$ with $e(x)<1$, $p_1(x)\in(0,1)$, $\Gamma>1$. Let $C_n(x)\subseteq[0,1]$ be the credal set an observed-data method reports after $n$ samples --- the interval hull of an ensemble fit to the selected units, or a high-posterior-mass interval --- with epistemic term $\mathrm{Epi}_n(x)=H(\bar p_n)-\tfrac1M\sum_mH(p_m)$, and let $\mathrm{Cens}(x)=\max_{q\in[\plo,\pup]}H(q)-\min_{q\in[\plo,\pup]}H(q)$ be the censoring term \eqref{eq:cens}. Call $C$ \emph{valid} at $x$ if it contains $p(x)$ under every law compatible with $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ and $P_{\mathrm{obs}}$. \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] \textup{(Never refuted.)} $\plo(x)<p_1(x)<\pup(x)$, and every compatible law induces the same $P_{\mathrm{obs}}$; hence no calibration, coverage or goodness-of-fit statistic of observed data has power above its size against the decomposition being biased. \item[(ii)] \textup{(Honest floor.)} $C$ is valid iff $C\supseteq[\plo,\pup]$; the smallest epistemic term any valid set can report is $\mathrm{Cens}(x)$, and for every $n$ \[ \mathrm{Bias}_n(x)\;:=\;\mathrm{EU}\big(\mathrm{hull}(C_n(x)\cup[\plo,\pup])\big)-\mathrm{Epi}_n(x) \;\ge\;\mathrm{Cens}(x)-\mathrm{Epi}_n(x), \] where $\mathrm{EU}(C)=\max_C H-\min_C H$ is the credal epistemic term. \item[(iii)] \textup{(Asymptotic overconfidence.)} If $C_n(x)$ contracts to $\{p_1(x)\}$ with Hausdorff radius $\varepsilon_n\to0$ --- a consistent posterior, or a converged ensemble of a well-specified class --- then $\mathrm{Epi}_n(x)\le H(\min\{2\varepsilon_n,\tfrac12\})\to0$ while $\mathrm{Bias}_n(x)\to\mathrm{Cens}(x)>0$: the reported epistemic term ends up $\mathrm{Cens}(x)-o(1)$ below that of \emph{every} valid credal set, and $\mathrm{Cens}(x)$ does not depend on $n$. \item[(iv)] \textup{(Size of the floor.)} With $m(x)=\min_{q\in[\plo,\pup]}|\logit q|$, \[ \mathrm{Cens}(x)\;\ge\;\delta(x)\,m(x)+\tfrac12\,\delta(x)^2, \qquad \delta(x)=\big(1-e(x)\big)\frac{\odds(p_1(x))\,(\Gamma^2-1)} {\big(1+\Gamma\odds(p_1(x))\big)\big(\Gamma+\odds(p_1(x))\big)}>0, \] and $\E_\mu[\mathrm{Cens}(X)]$ equals the width of the sharp identified interval for the population aleatoric entropy $\E_\mu[H(p(X))]$. \end{enumerate} The full statement, a plug-in version with cross-fitted nuisances (\cref{prop:cens-plugin}), and proofs are in \cref{app:uq}.

def:valid.title: Valid credal set, reported and honest epistemic terms
def:valid.text: Fix $x$. A closed set $C\subseteq[0,1]$ is \emph{valid at $x$ under $\dcsm(\Gamma)$} if $p(x)\in C$ for every law $P$ that satisfies $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ and induces the observed law $P_{\mathrm{obs}}$. An \emph{observed-data method} returns, for each $n$, a credal set $C_n(x)\subseteq[0,1]$ built from $O_1,\dots,O_n$ --- the interval hull of an ensemble $\{p^{(n)}_m(x)\}_{m\le M}$ fit to the selected units, or the support of a posterior over $p_\theta(x)$ --- and reports the two-way decomposition \[ \mathrm{Tot}_n(x)=H(\bar p_n(x)),\qquad \mathrm{Ale}_n(x)=\tfrac1M\textstyle\sum_m H(p^{(n)}_m(x)),\qquad \mathrm{Epi}_n(x)=\mathrm{Tot}_n(x)-\mathrm{Ale}_n(x), \] with $\bar p_n=\tfrac1M\sum_m p^{(n)}_m$ (posterior expectations in the Bayesian case). The \emph{honest epistemic term} of the method is the credal epistemic term of the smallest set that is both consistent with its own sampling spread and valid, $\mathrm{EU}\big(\mathrm{hull}(C_n(x)\cup\I_\Gamma(x))\big)$, and its \emph{bias} is \begin{equation} \mathrm{Bias}_n(x)\;:=\;\mathrm{EU}\big(\mathrm{hull}(C_n(x)\cup\I_\Gamma(x))\big)\;-\;\mathrm{Epi}_n(x). \end{equation}

cor:uq-full.title: Full statement of \cref{cor:uq}
cor:uq-full.text: Assume $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ and fix $x$ with $e(x)<1$, $p_1(x)\in(0,1)$ and $\Gamma>1$ (otherwise $\delta(x)=0$ and every quantity below is $0$). Then: \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] \textup{(The naive answer is never refuted.)} $\plo(x)<p_1(x)<\pup(x)$. The selection-on-observables law $P^{(1)}$ (tilt $a\equiv1$, so $p=p_1$) satisfies $\dcsm(\Gamma)$ for every $\Gamma\ge1$ and induces the same $P_{\mathrm{obs}}$; consequently every statistic $S(O_1,\dots,O_n)$ has the same distribution under every admissible law. In particular no calibration, coverage or goodness-of-fit test computed on observed data has power above its size against ``$\mathrm{Epi}_n$ understates the epistemic uncertainty about $p(x)$''. \item[(ii)] \textup{(The honest floor and a finite-$n$ inequality.)} $C$ is valid at $x$ iff $C\supseteq\I_\Gamma(x)$, and \[ \inf\{\mathrm{EU}(C):\ C\ \text{valid at }x\}\;=\;\mathrm{EU}(\I_\Gamma(x))\;=\;\mathrm{Cens}(x), \] attained by $C=\I_\Gamma(x)$. For every $n$ and every observed-data method, $0\le\mathrm{Epi}_n(x)\le\mathrm{EU}(C_n(x))$ and \begin{equation} \mathrm{Bias}_n(x)\;\ge\;\max\big\{\mathrm{EU}(C_n(x)),\ \mathrm{Cens}(x)\big\}-\mathrm{Epi}_n(x) \;\ge\;\mathrm{Cens}(x)-\mathrm{Epi}_n(x). \end{equation} \item[(iii)] \textup{(Asymptotic overconfidence.)} Let $\varepsilon_n(x)=\sup_{q\in C_n(x)}|q-p_1(x)|$ and suppose $\varepsilon_n(x)\to0$ (almost surely, or in probability; the conclusions then hold in the same mode) --- as for a consistent posterior or a converged ensemble of a well-specified class. Then \[ \mathrm{Epi}_n(x)\;\le\;H\big(\min\{2\varepsilon_n(x),\tfrac12\}\big)\;\longrightarrow\;0, \qquad \mathrm{Cens}(x)-\mathrm{Epi}_n(x)\;\le\;\mathrm{Bias}_n(x)\;\le\; \mathrm{Cens}(x)+2H\big(\min\{\varepsilon_n(x),\tfrac12\}\big)-\mathrm{Epi}_n(x), \] so $\mathrm{Bias}_n(x)\to\mathrm{Cens}(x)>0$. Precisely: \emph{``asymptotically overconfident by at least $\mathrm{Cens}(x)$'' means} \begin{equation} \liminf_{n\to\infty}\ \inf_{C\ \mathrm{valid\ at}\ x}\big[\mathrm{EU}(C)-\mathrm{Epi}_n(x)\big] \;=\;\lim_{n\to\infty}\big[\mathrm{Cens}(x)-\mathrm{Epi}_n(x)\big]\;=\;\mathrm{Cens}(x), \end{equation} i.e.\ for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $n_0$ such that for all $n\ge n_0$ the reported epistemic term is at least $\mathrm{Cens}(x)-\epsilon$ below the epistemic term of \emph{every} valid credal set, while $\mathrm{Cens}(x)$ itself does not depend on $n$. \item[(iv)] \textup{(Explicit form of the censoring term.)} With $d(x)=\max\{\tfrac12-\plo(x),\ \pup(x)-\tfrac12\}$, \begin{align} \tfrac12\notin\I_\Gamma(x):&\quad \mathrm{Cens}(x)=\Big|\int_{\plo(x)}^{\pup(x)}\logit q\,dq\Big| \;\ge\;\delta(x)\,m(x)+2\,\delta(x)^2,\qquad \mathrm{Cens}(x)\le\delta(x)\max_{q\in\I_\Gamma(x)}|\logit q|; \\ \tfrac12\in\I_\Gamma(x):&\quad \mathrm{Cens}(x)=\log2-\min\{H(\plo),H(\pup)\} =\KL\big(\mathrm{Bern}(q^\ast)\,\|\,\mathrm{Bern}(\tfrac12)\big) \;\ge\;2\,d(x)^2\;\ge\;\tfrac12\,\delta(x)^2, \end{align} where $q^\ast$ is the endpoint of $\I_\Gamma(x)$ farther from $\tfrac12$. In both cases \begin{equation} \mathrm{Cens}(x)\;\ge\;\delta(x)\,m(x)+\tfrac12\,\delta(x)^2, \qquad \delta(x)=\big(1-e(x)\big)\,\frac{\odds(p_1(x))\,(\Gamma^2-1)} {\big(1+\Gamma\,\odds(p_1(x))\big)\big(\Gamma+\odds(p_1(x))\big)}\;>\;0 . \end{equation} \item[(v)] \textup{(Mean version.)} $\E_\mu[\mathrm{Cens}(X)]=\E_\mu[\overline h(X)]-\E_\mu[\underline h(X)]$ is exactly the width of the sharp identified interval for the population aleatoric entropy $\E_\mu[H(p(X))]$ (endpoints $\overline h=H(\mathrm{clip}_{[\plo,\pup]}(\tfrac12))$, $\underline h=\min\{H(\plo),H(\pup)\}$, both attained). For every $n$, $\E_\mu[\mathrm{Bias}_n(X)]\ge\E_\mu[\mathrm{Cens}(X)]-\E_\mu[\mathrm{Epi}_n(X)]$; if the hypothesis of (iii) holds for $\mu$-a.e.\ $x$ then $\E_\mu[\mathrm{Epi}_n(X)]\to0$ and $\E_\mu[\mathrm{Bias}_n(X)]\to\E_\mu[\mathrm{Cens}(X)]$, with \begin{equation} \E_\mu[\mathrm{Cens}(X)]\;\ge\;\E_\mu[\delta(X)\,m(X)]+\tfrac12\E_\mu[\delta(X)^2] \;\ge\;\E_\mu[\delta(X)\,m(X)]+\tfrac12\,(\pi_+-\pi_-)^2, \end{equation} $\pi_\pm=\E_\mu[\pup],\E_\mu[\plo]$ the prevalence interval of \cref{thm:sharp-auc}. \end{enumerate}

prop:cens-plugin.title: Plug-in censoring term with cross-fitted nuisances
prop:cens-plugin.text: Let $\hat\plo,\hat\pup$ be the box built from cross-fitted $(\hat e,\hat\eta_1)$ and $\widehat{\mathrm{Cens}}(x)=\mathrm{EU}([\hat\plo(x),\hat\pup(x)])$. With $\Delta_n(x)=|\hat e(x)-e(x)|+\tfrac14|\hat\eta_1(x)-\eta_1(x)|$, \begin{equation} \big|\widehat{\mathrm{Cens}}(x)-\mathrm{Cens}(x)\big|\;\le\;2\,H\big(\min\{\Delta_n(x),\tfrac12\}\big) \;\le\;2\,\Delta_n(x)\big(1+\log\tfrac1{\Delta_n(x)}\big), \end{equation} and, with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{nuis}}=\|\hat e-e\|_{L^1(\mu)}+\tfrac14\|\hat\eta_1-\eta_1\|_{L^1(\mu)}$ as in \cref{cor:loggamma}, $\E_\mu\big|\widehat{\mathrm{Cens}}(X)-\mathrm{Cens}(X)\big|\le 2H(\min\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{nuis}},\tfrac12\})$. Moreover the inflated box $\I^{+}_n(x)=[\hat\plo(x)-\Delta_n(x),\ \hat\pup(x)+\Delta_n(x)]\cap[0,1]$ contains $\I_\Gamma(x)$, so it is valid at $x$ and $\mathrm{EU}(\I^{+}_n(x))\ge\mathrm{Cens}(x)$; replacing $\Delta_n(x)$ by any radius $r_n(x)\ge\Delta_n(x)$ that holds with probability $1-\alpha$ gives a valid floor at level $1-\alpha$.
